concepts.why: The patient presented with abdominal pain that localized to the right lower quadrant, had a positive Rovsing sign, and had lobulated tubular soft tissue and inflammation adjacent to the terminal ileum/ileocecal valve on CT scan.
The patient had a history of endometriosis and biopsy of inflamed areas demonstrated foci of endometriosis.
The patient had a repeat white-cell count of 13.2×10^9/L and repeat CT showed small-bowel obstruction at the terminal ileum, likely secondary to an adjacent pericecal soft-tissue mass.

The patient had a presumptive diagnosis of acute appendicitis, but the appendix was not identified on CT scan and diagnostic laparoscopy showed no appendix despite full mobilization of the cecum and small-bowel run.
The patient had a pericecal soft-tissue mass on CT scan, which could be a neoplasm.
The patient had a history of endometriosis and biopsy of inflamed areas demonstrated foci of endometriosis.
The patient had a presumptive diagnosis of acute appendicitis and had lobulated tubular soft tissue and inflammation adjacent to the terminal ileum/ileocecal valve on CT scan.
The patient had mild inflammatory changes of the terminal ileum and adhesions on diagnostic laparoscopy.

rationales.F01: Intermittent throbbing abdominal pain is a non-specific symptom.
rationales.F02: Pain localizing to the right lower quadrant is suggestive of appendicitis or other conditions affecting the terminal ileum.
rationales.F04: Moderate tenderness in the right lower quadrant is consistent with appendicitis or other inflammatory conditions.
rationales.F05: A positive Rovsing sign is indicative of appendicitis.
rationales.F07: Lobulated tubular soft tissue and inflammation adjacent to the terminal ileum/ileocecal valve is highly suggestive of appendicitis.
rationales.F08: The absence of an identified appendix on imaging does not rule out appendicitis, especially if the appendix is retrocecal or inverted.
rationales.F10: Biopsy findings of acute inflammation and foci of endometriosis suggest intestinal endometriosis.
rationales.F12: Small-bowel obstruction at the terminal ileum, likely secondary to an adjacent pericecal soft-tissue mass, is consistent with several conditions including neoplasm or inverted appendix.
